slot.brief: Charge sharing: two capacitors at different voltages connected in parallel; compute common voltage and energy lost as heat, comparing initial and final stored energies.

stem: A $2\ \mu$F capacitor at $6$ V and a $4\ \mu$F capacitor at $3$ V are connected in parallel with like terminals together. How much energy is lost during charge sharing?

verdicts.working: Initial charge: 2×6 + 4×3 = 24 μC. Final voltage = 24/6 = 4 V. Initial energy = 54 μJ; final energy = 48 μJ, so 6 μJ is lost.

working:
$V_f=\dfrac{C_1V_1+C_2V_2}{C_1+C_2}=\dfrac{2(6)+4(3)}{6}=4$ V
$U_i=\dfrac12[2(6^2)+4(3^2)]=54\ \mu$J
$U_f=\dfrac12(6)(4^2)=48\ \mu$J
$\Delta U=U_i-U_f=6\ \mu$J

Independent check: Initial charge: 2×6 + 4×3 = 24 μC. Final voltage = 24/6 = 4 V. Initial energy = 54 μJ; final energy = 48 μJ, so 6 μJ is lost.
solution:
Charge is conserved, so the common final voltage is
$$V_f=\frac{C_1V_1+C_2V_2}{C_1+C_2}=\frac{2(6)+4(3)}{6}=4\text{ V}.$$
The energy lost is $U_i-U_f=\frac12[2(6^2)+4(3^2)]-\frac12(6)(4^2)=54-48=6\,\mu\text{J}$.The final result is $6\,\mu\text{J}$.
